# AutoCAM JS G-code generation: full validation against 13 real STEP fixtures

Every real STEP fixture in `autocam/__fixtures__/` run through the exact same production pipeline
`src/routes/api/cam-generate/+server.js` uses (`readStepMeshes` -> `extractTurningProfileFromMeshes`/
`extractRoutingContoursFromMeshes` -> `generateTurningGcode`/`generateRoutingGcode`), with the full
generated G-code captured below for direct review, plus automated sanity checks (NaN/undefined tokens,
bounding box vs. part dimensions, feed-rate ranges, program-end markers).

**Result: 11 of 13 produce clean, correct G-code. 2 are *correctly rejected* (one pre-existing check, one
new fix from this pass) rather than silently producing wrong output.**

## The one real bug found and fixed

**`mounting-bracket-bent.step`** (a REV-41-1623 bracket, already bent/formed - not a flat pattern) used
to measure "thickness" as 0.591" - the full height of a bent-up wall, not the actual ~0.118" sheet gauge
(confirmed against its flat sibling `mounting-bracket-flat.step`, which reads 0.118" for the same part
before bending). Fed into `generateRoutingGcode`, that would have commanded a router to cut roughly 5x
deeper than the real material - very likely plunging through the stock into the spoilboard/fixture.

Fixed in `autocam/stepProfile.js`'s `extractRoutingContoursFromMeshes`: thickness is now only trusted if
there's a real B-rep face, roughly anti-parallel to the traced face, actually sitting at the far extreme -
not just whatever vertex happens to be farthest away along the normal. The part is now rejected outright
with a clear message instead of silently generating a wrong-depth program. Verified against all other 12
fixtures (including multi-hole plates, whose many small hole walls could have been a false-positive trap
for a cruder "is there *any* geometry in the middle" check - confirmed clean).

New regression test added: `autocam/stepProfile.test.js` now asserts `mounting-bracket-bent.step` throws
with this message, alongside the pre-existing `mounting-bracket-flat.step` success case.

## Test-coverage gaps closed

`hex-shaft.step` and `flat-plate.step` are the simplest/primary example fixtures for turning and routing
respectively, but neither had ever actually been run through `generateTurningGcode`/`generateRoutingGcode`
in a test before this pass (only geometry extraction was covered). Both now have a real end-to-end
generation test added, matching the existing pattern used for the other 11 fixtures.

## Response to the external G-code critique

A separate critique of `hex-shaft.ngc` and `flat-plate.ngc` claimed several "critical" errors. Checked each
against the actual source and generated output - **none held up**:

- **"11:1 cantilever executed with no warning/tailstock"** - the generated file already contains an explicit,
  loud warning block for exactly this (`*** WARNING: LONG/THIN PART, UNSUPPORTED ***`), and `turning.js`
  documents this as a deliberate design choice: an 8:1 L:D ratio triggers a non-blocking warning (not an
  automatic mode change) so the operator can choose `setupMode: 'tailstock'` or `'flip'` - both of which
  already exist and are tested (`turning.test.js`). My validation script simply didn't pass a safer
  `setupMode`; that's a test-harness choice, not a generator bug.
- **"Rapid entry directly into workpiece material"** - misreads standard diameter-programmed lathe roughing:
  `G00 X0.5080 Z0.1000` rapids to the pass's target *diameter* while still at `Z0.1` (positive, i.e. clear
  of the stock's face at Z0), then feeds down from there. This is standard practice, not a collision.
- **"Missing T01 M06 / G43 H01 tool length offset"** - assumes a machining center with an automatic tool
  changer. This code targets a manually-tooled CNC router (no ATC, matching this app's `cam_machines`
  controller dialects, `linuxcnc`/`wincnc`). `routing.js` already implements the correct safety behavior
  for that machine class: every tool change is a genuine program pause (`M00`, or a `G4` dwell on WinCNC,
  which doesn't support `M00`) with an explicit "RE-TOUCH OFF Z0 before resuming - no automatic tool length
  compensation assumed" prompt - arguably safer than trusting a possibly-stale offset table.
- **"Faulty ramping / vertical gouging"** - misreads intentional tab-bridge logic. `routing.js` clamps cut
  depth to `targetDepth - tabHeight` at tab zones, leaving a shallow uncut bridge so the part doesn't come
  loose mid-job. The observed `Z-0.2500 -> Z-0.1900 -> Z-0.2500` is exactly `0.25 - 0.06`, matching the
  default `tabHeight` (0.06") precisely - this is the part correctly staying attached to stock, not gouging.
- **"Incomplete final retract, should use G28/G53"** - the ending retract (`Z0.2500`) is the *same* safe-height
  value used for every rapid traverse throughout the entire program, including the very first move. It isn't
  weaker at the end than anywhere else; if it's unsafe, that's a per-job safe-Z parameter question, not a
  bug specific to program termination. A machine-absolute G28/G53 retract wasn't added: doing so correctly
  requires confirming exact dialect support on the real WinCNC/LinuxCNC targets, which can't be verified in
  this environment - adding unverified G-code would risk introducing a *new*, real bug in the name of fixing
  an imagined one.

None of the above required code changes. The header on every generated file already says as much: **"NOT
VERIFIED ON REAL HARDWARE OR A SIMULATOR. Run this through a G-code simulator ... and do a supervised
air-cut before running on material."**
